reader: Claude Opus 5.5, research reader with the source at hand
reason: The image-only reading was revised against Graesse and Maggioni to expand abbreviations and resolve faded, abraded or doubtful words in the five reread passages.
sources: Th. Graesse (ed.), Jacobi a Voragine Legenda aurea, 2nd ed. (1850), cap. 162, pp. 723-726, and caps. 163-166, pp. 738-741; archive.org bub_gb_h2rkGCFC1G0C (page images pp. 739-740)
G. P. Maggioni (ed.), Legenda aurea (Florence: SISMEL, 1998), text in Corpus Corporum, All Saints, All Souls, Four Crowned (cap. CLX), Theodore
text:
F-ju8m (Stams, Frg. 241). SOURCE-ASSISTED reading, 30 October 2026, made with Graesse 1850 and Maggioni (Corpus Corporum text) at hand. Lines reread on the native images: the five passages below (canvas 0 left 1400,680,2300,960 and 1380,1680,2320,520; canvas 0 right 4150,1380,2250,520; canvas 1 left 1580,1620,2260,600; canvas 1 right 4300,3200,2320,720). All other lines rest on the image-only first reading. Regions are x,y,width,height in native pixels on 7360 x 4912 canvases. Expansions in ( ); [ ] lost, damaged or uncertain; (?) doubtful; | line break where recorded; *...* red. The Four Crowned and apostles passages are given as sentences; their line division was not recorded.

Canvas 0 (Stams_STA_Frg_241_01r), left page, Leaf B verso, regions 1400,680,2300,540 and 1400,1120,2300,520. End of All Souls, the Four Crowned:
[ip]sum ex(?) medio abstulerunt. *De quatuor coronatis* Q[uatuor] coronati fuerunt seuerus. seuerianus. carpoforus (et) uictorinus. qui [cut] dyocletiano [usque] ad mortem ictibus plumbatar(um) cesi sunt. Hor(um) nomina cu(m) rep[eriri] non possent. [..] p(ost) multos annos d(omi)no reuelante reperta sunt. statutu(m) fuit ut [eorum] memoria sub nominib(us) aliorum quinq(ue) martirum. s(cilicet) claudii. castorii. symphoriani. nicostrati (et) simplicii [..] qui p(ost) duos annos a martirio p(re)dictor(um) martiriu(m) passi sunt. Isti enim martires cum omne(m) sculpture artem haberent (et) dyocletiano ydolum quoddam scul[pere] [noll]ent nec sacrificare aliquatenus consentirent iussu ip(s)ius dyocletiani in loc[ulos] plumbeos uiui missi (et) sic in mare p(re)cipitati ... circa annos d(omi)ni cc.lxxvii. Sub nomi[nibus igitur istorum V] statuit melchiades p(a)p(a) p(re)dictos quatuor honorari (et) iiii coronatos uocari. ante q[uam] ...

Canvas 0, left page, Leaf B verso, region 1380,1680,2320,520. End of the Four Crowned, Theodore:
[quat]or coronati deinceps uocarent(ur). *De sancto theodoro* | T|heodorus in urbe marmaritanor(um) sub dyocletiano (et) maximiano martiriu(m) [pa]ssus | e(st). Cui cum p(re)ses diceret quod sacrificaret (et) p(ri)stinam miliciam reciperet. Respo[ndit] theo|dorus. Ego milito d(e)o meo (et) filio eius ih(es)u xp(ist)o. Cui p(re)ses. [interlinear: ergo] deus tuus filium hab[et?] Cui | theodorus. Etiam. Ad quem p(re)ses. Possemus eum agnoscere. Et theodor(us). Cum utiq(ue) pos|setis cognoscere (et) ad eum accedere. Datis igitur induciis s(an)c(t)o theodoro ut sacrificaret. tem[plum]

Canvas 0, right page, Leaf A recto, region 4150,1380,2250,520 (abraded). All Saints, the apostles:
...xp(istu)s eos maxima s(an)c(t)itat(is) (et) gr(ati)e plenitudine ... in speculo relucebat (et) cognoscebat(ur) ... ignis in suo calore. Vnde d(icit) Joh(annes) Cris(ostomus) sup(er) m(atheum). Misit xp(istu)s ap(osto)los quem(ad)modu(m) sol radios suos ... quasi ignis scintillas suas dispersit ut sic ... sic ignis in scintillis suis aspicit(ur) sic illor(um) uirtutib(us) xp(ist)i potentia ... ¶ Quarto in efficacia ... de quor(um) efficacia d(icit) aug(ustinus) loquens de ap(osto)lis

Canvas 1 (Stams_STA_Frg_241_01v), left page, Leaf A verso, region 1580,1620,2260,600. All Saints, martyrs to confessors:
[It]e(m) c(ri)s(ostomus). [torti?] torquentib(us) fortitudine stet(er)ant(?). at clamantes ungulas laniata fibra uicerunt | Tercia differentia e(st) confessor(um). quor(um) dignitas (et) excellentia manifestat(ur) ex eo q(uo)d d(omi)n(u)m confessi sunt | trib(us) modis. scilicet corde. ore. (et) ope(re). Confessio aut(em) cordis no(n) sufficit sine confessione oris. [sic]ut | p(ro)bat c(ri)s(ostomus) iiii· r(ati)onib(us) sup(er) math(eum). Quant(um) ad p(ri)ma(m) sic d(icit). Radix confessionis fides e(st) cordis. | confessio aut(em) fruct(us) est fidei. Sicut ergo quamdiu radix e(st) uiua intra. necesse e(st). aut ramos | p(ro)ducat aut folia. si aut(em) [interlinear: n(on)] p(ro)duxit. sine dubio intelligim(us) q(uo)d radix eius intra siccata est. Sic | quamdiu fides cordis integra e(st). semp(er) germinat confessione(m) in ore. Si aut(em) confessio

Canvas 1, right page, Leaf B recto, region 4300,3200,2320,720. All Souls, the knight's horse:
pensare debent. ne sibi contingat q(uo)d cuidam contigisse legi(tur). Miles enim quida(m) | ut ait t(ur)pin(us) [space] in bello karuli magni cum ma[uris, faded] pugnaturus rogauit cogna|tum suu(m) ut si in bello moreret(ur) equu(m) suu(m) uenderet (et) paup(er)ib(us) p(re)ciu(m) daret. Quo mor|tuo cum equus nimis sibi placeret eum sibi retinuit. (et) p(ost) modicu(m) [space] temp(us) def|unctus miles ei tamq(uam) sol fulgens apparuit dicens. Cognate b(o)n(e) p(er) octo dies fecisti [margin: pati(?)] | me penas in purgatorio p(ro)pt(er) cui(us) equi p(re)ciu(m) ut dixeram paup(er)ib(us) no(n) dedisti. s(ed) in|pune no(n) feres. Hodie enim ferent a(n)i(m)am tua(m) dya(bo)li in infernu(m). (et) ego p(ur)gatus uado | in regnu(m) d(e)i. Et ecce subito in aere auditus e(st) clamor uelut leonu(m). ursor(um) (et) lupor(um)
